pr_comments: I can't update the hidden-definitions `.rbi` file because I'm on an M1 Mac. That should fix the CI syntax failures.
Only remaining issue is that I can't update the hidden-definitions `.rbi` file because I'm on an M1 Mac. Any workaround for this?

I just pushed a change adding those lines (you can still make those changes but, yeah, I guess you can't test them out on an M1).

I also updated the manages and completions while I was at it

> I just pushed a change adding those lines (you can still make those changes but, yeah, I guess you can't test them out on an M1).

Do you make those changes manually or with `brew typecheck --update`? Also, does BrewTestBot update the manpages and completions or is that something a contributor should do when changing commands/flags?

> I'm not opposed to this but it does seem almost identical to `brew autoremove -n`. I guess there probably is a benefit to having these in this command as well, but it definitely feels like the logic could be shared between them.

I agree. Took note of duplicated logic between them in initial PR message and meant to revisit. Do you think it would be worth defining an `installed_as_dependency?` instance method on `Formula`?

> Do you make those changes manually or with `brew typecheck --update`?

Good question, I actually didn't know about `brew typecheck --update` until now, so I could be off a bit on this explanation. We have two types of RBI files in the brew repo. We have some files (like [`Library/Homebrew/cli/args.rbi`](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/Library/Homebrew/cli/args.rbi)) that are ways for us to specify type information for internal stuff (like we need to do when adding new methods in here).

We also have RBI files that define the methods that exist on our dependencies (see the humongous [`Library/Homebrew/sorbet/rbi/hidden-definitions/hidden.rbi`](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/Library/Homebrew/sorbet/rbi/hidden-definitions/hidden.rbi) file. As the gems we depend on are updated, this file sometimes needs updates to match the updated gems. This is what `brew typecheck --update` is for. I don't know how it works, but it looks through the dependencies and updates that `hidden-definitions.rbi` file (possibly among other things) to match and ensure we have up-to-date type information for all gems. So in this case, running that makes a bunch of changes to `hidden-definitions.rbi` but none actually fix the internal issues of the `installed_as_*?` methods not being known to the type checker.

This is done automatically by the [`sorbet`](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/master/.github/workflows/sorbet.yml) GitHub actions workflow, so it's not really designed for manual use.

There's also `brew typecheck --fix` which _is_ designed to be a user-run command, but this also wouldn't have solved the problem. I think that it assumes that the type information that it has is correct, so any `brew typecheck` violations are assumed to be mistakes by the contributor rather than indicating that type information needs to be updated. That must be done manually. If you had run `brew typecheck --fix` it wouldn't have done anything in this case.

Hope that made sense

> Also, does BrewTestBot update the manpages and completions or is that something a contributor should do when changing commands/flags?

The `brew generate-man-completions` command is used to generate these. I can't remember if it works on M1 yet or not. It is done automatically as a follow-up PR so you're definitely not required to run it on every PR. Most of the time it doesn't actually result in any changes. It used to be required for PRs to be merged so it's part of my typical `brew style`/`brew typecheck`/`brew generate-man-completions`/`brew tests` workflow that I use, so the reason I did here was really just that it was just done automatically 😅

So: no, don't worry about it but you certainly can if you'd like.

issue_context.title: Follow manually installed packages and automatically installed dependencies separately
issue_context.body:
### Provide a detailed description of the proposed feature

Have a command similar to `brew leaves` which shows all the packages manually installed by the user themselves, without various automatically installed dependencies. `brew leaves` shows only packages which aren't dependencies of anything, even if the user installed them manually (e.g. if Python 3.9 is installed manually by the user, it's often also a dependency and doesn't show up there).

### What is the motivation for the feature?

Standard functionality in other package managers (e.g. apt has `apt-mark showmanual`, `apt-mark markauto`)

### How will the feature be relevant to at least 90% of Homebrew users?

They can easily differentiate between the 80% of installed packages which are automatic dependencies and packages they installed themselves and want to keep

### What alternatives to the feature have been considered?

Manually keeping a text file of what packages I've installed
comments: `brew bundle dump` will generate a `Brewfile` listing all the formulae (and casks) you've installed on request.

That's good, but not quite a fit. To be specific about the feature request, three commands would be required:
- `brew showmanual` - shows all currently installed packages which have been set to manually installed
- `brew markmanual` - marks an automatically installed dependency as manually installed
- `brew markauto` - marks a manually installed packages as an automatically installed dependency, and uninstalls if no other package depends on it

>shows all currently installed packages which have been set to manually installed

`brew bundle dump`

>marks an automatically installed dependency as manually installed

Add it to your `Brewfile`

>marks a manually installed packages as an automatically installed dependency, and uninstalls if no other package depends on it

Make sure your `Brewfile` is correctly specified, then run `brew bundle cleanup --force`
Yeah, I'm sure you understand that's not quite proper ergonomics for the use case

> * `brew markmanual` - marks an automatically installed dependency as manually installed

`brew install` already does this if the package is already installed.

> * `brew markauto` - marks a manually installed packages as an automatically installed dependency, and uninstalls if no other package depends on it

This requires manually editing the `INSTALL_RECEIPT.json`. I'm not sure I've seen enough demand to warrant adding a new command for it (but an external command [https://docs.brew.sh/External-Commands] could be added for this).

> * `brew showmanual` - shows all currently installed packages which have been set to manually installed

`brew leaves --installed-on-request` and `brew leaves --not-installed-as-dependency` could be added as flags which use these entries for identification. Marking this as the "help wanted" here.

Similar funcctionality [was suggested](https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/pull/1881#issuecomment-274260312) as complementary to #1881's '`brew orphaned`' at the time.  (That command never got implemented even though '`brew autoremove`' did.  Some of the code used to implement the latter should help.)

Wow! This is fantastic! You actually implemented my feature request! I do hope you guys understand that Homebrew is probably the most valuable open source tool I use on my macOS and the work you guys do is awesome. I put in a little monetary sponsorship via Github. Thank you so much for Homebrew, you guys rock!! ❤️ 

@MikeMcQuaid @RandomDSdevel @Rylan12 @cnnrmnn
Better still @tonimelisma: a community member (@cnnrmnn) implemented it rather than one of the maintainers. He rocks, you rock, everyone rocks! 🎉 🎸 👨🏻‍🎤 👩🏻‍🎤
